findings.reason: the before-figure the section rests on cannot be produced by the rule it names, so either the ported rule must be decoupled from JSON encoding (detect the replace call regardless of payload) or the done-when must drop them; the first implementation node would otherwise spend its gate reconciling an instrument that structurally cannot pass it.
findings.text: §9 describes the census rule it will port as "matching os.replace, os.rename and a one-argument .replace or .rename attribute call", but in the census that detection is nested inside the `JSON document encoding` branch (docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233, the appended concept at :260-272) and appends "Atomic JSON file replacement" only when the same function also calls `json.dump`/`json.dumps`. The two serve.py publishers the plan names as load-bearing cases write raw bytes and call `temporary.replace(destination)` with no json call in the same function — `reckon/serve.py:503` (client asset) and `reckon/serve.py:567` (compiled JSX) — so the ported rule, whether copied verbatim or implemented as the plan describes it, would not flag them; yet §9's done-when asserts the base-revision inventory reports "every site in the inventory above, the four in serve.py included", and §9 requires exactly two functions at the head including the non-json directory rename in `reckon/resources.py`. The instrument and the completion test disagree.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 promotes one primitive whose `render(handle)` callback signature hides temporary naming and uniqueness, chmod-versus-umask mode handling, file and directory fsync, and failure cleanup behind a single call; the two modules below it (`project_state.py`, `crew/follow_checkpoint.py`) shrink rather than grow.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §9 names `reckon/interface_counts.py` as the runtime owner to extend and rejects `reckon/clones.py:functions_in` with a verified reason (`functions_in` returns token windows in `_Function.tokens` and holds no call, reckon/clones.py:172-196), and the census under `docs/research` is a frozen artifact a package caller cannot import.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 and §9 each name their one added public definition and state that the retired forks are underscore-private and uncounted, and a promoted primitive with no duplicate site cannot shrink the family, and §7 adds no surface (it rewrites one expression at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:3844`).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the codebase and cites the mechanisms it extends (`reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary`, `reckon/interface_counts.py:read_trees`/`definitions`, and the census's `primitive_concepts`), but its account of the census rule it means to port is inaccurate, so the instrument it proposes cannot report the sites its own done-when requires.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 promotes an existing private primitive by renaming it public rather than layering a new one over it, and §9 requires a site needing behaviour the primitive lacks to extend the primitive once under a keyword argument rather than wrap it.
